study.question: Can the rank96 incumbent retain its click-quality/storage advantage and gain reproducible prediction efficiency by transferring the existing fused evaluation path, and does rank reduction contribute runtime savings once both ranks use that path?
study.hypothesis: Observation: balanced112->96 raised single-seed click AUC0.6674485580556159->0.6675003890552496 and reduced dense Parameters205427->200563, but native p50 changed only15.22645->15.19727ms. At full112, archived fused prediction preserved click AUC and measured15.03076ms versus15.10102ms native, while product-only folding measured15.25480ms. Mechanism hypothesis: capacity and execution form are separate bottlenecks. Recompose the buy-context factors each evaluation call and fuse their map with existing semantic local weights, removing an intermediate batch matrix while retaining the rank-constrained training pathway. Reduced rank may save storage but no longer appreciably save prediction work after both ranks are fused. These are provisional explanations; historical timing is noisy and no candidate outcome is known. Freeze before execution: utility preservation requires validation click AUC >=0.6674003890552496 (at most0.000100 absolute below the current incumbent0.6675003890552496), also exceeding the imported joint reference0.666753547526167 minus0.000100. This stronger incumbent gate supersedes only this study's prospective selection criterion, never the frozen scorer/protocol. It does not retroactively relabel older trials. Select by validation only. At fixed rank, changing buy evaluation must leave click/cart/fav predictions exactly unchanged at the same checkpoint. All auxiliary AUC/Logloss and mean auxiliary AUC must be reported separately; rank96 already loses cart/fav/buy AUC relative to full112, so click preservation cannot be called joint-task preservation. Freeze cost gate: a useful combined candidate must retain4864 fewer trainable Parameters than full112 and reduce whole-model p50 latency by at least1% against same-rank native, with p95 no more than1% worse and end-to-end inference seconds lower under matched conditions. Also compare fused96 against fused112; any common fusion gain belongs to implementation, not rank. One timed validation pass is screening evidence only. A supported cost claim requires at least three matched timing passes per configuration if the host later authorizes replay of these validation inputs, reporting medians/ranges with identical warm-up; otherwise mark cost unresolved. Do not claim training speed benefit from an evaluation-only switch.
